title: Lying-Down Release Practice
description: Players lie on their backs and shoot the ball straight up so it lands back in the shooting hand — an isolated drill for backspin and a straight release.

content.objective: Feel a straight, one-hand release with even backspin, without the distractions of the rim and legs.
content.setup: Players lie on their backs on the floor, spread out, a ball each.
content.organization: Whole group; also an at-home exercise.
instructions: Lie on the back with knees bent, ball in the shooting hand above the shoulder.
Elbow points to the ceiling, under the ball.
Shoot the ball straight up about one metre with a wrist snap.
Catch it with the same hand and repeat.
Check the spin: the seams should rotate straight backward.
coachingPoints: Straight up and straight down: if it drifts, the elbow is out.
Snap the wrist, fingers finish pointing up.
commonMistakes: Pushing the ball with two hands.
Flicking with the fingers only, no elbow extension.
content.safety: Shoot only a metre high so the ball cannot hit faces; spread players out.
progressions: Close the eyes on the last five reps.
regressions: Shoot to a partner kneeling beside you.
variations: Standing version against a wall target.
successCriteria: Ten reps in a row landing back in the hand.
Straight backspin seen on most reps.
content.gameApplication: A straight release with backspin gives the ball a soft touch on the rim.
